title: A quarter of young Africans believe USAID cuts could be positive, survey finds

paragraphs.en: A quarter of young Africans believe aid cuts by the US could have a positive impact, saying that losing foreign money will force leaders to confront and solve their own challenges, according to a new survey.
paragraphs.zh: 一项最新调查显示，四分之一的非洲年轻人认为美国削减援助可能产生积极影响，他们表示，失去外国资金将迫使本国领导人正视并解决自身的挑战。

paragraphs.en: In Ghana and Nigeria, almost half (41% and 40% respectively) of young people aged 18 to 24 were optimistic, with Liberia not far behind (37%). A further one in 10 (11%) young people were uncertain about the impact, according to the African Youth Survey, which interviewed almost 5,000 people across 16 of the continent’s 54 recognised countries.
paragraphs.zh: 在加纳和尼日利亚，几乎一半（分别为41%和40%）18至24岁的年轻人持乐观态度，利比里亚紧随其后（37%）。根据非洲青年调查的数据，另有十分之一（11%）的年轻人对影响不确定。该调查采访了非洲54个公认国家中16个国家的近5000人。

paragraphs.en: The Trump administration announced in early 2025 that it was eliminating more than 90% of USAID’s foreign contracts and $60bn in overall US assistance around the world. US foreign aid had been designed to play a critical role in tackling poverty, hunger and inequality worldwide.
paragraphs.zh: 特朗普政府于2025年初宣布，将取消美国国际开发署（USAID）90%以上的对外合同，以及美国在全球范围内总计600亿美元的援助。美国对外援助本应在解决全球贫困、饥饿和不平等方面发挥关键作用。

paragraphs.en: Other countries, including Britain, France and Germany, have also been slashing aid budgets. The UK announced in February 2025 that the aid budget would be cut from 0.5% of gross national income to 0.3% in 2027, its lowest level as a percentage of national income since records began. The UN target is 0.7%.
paragraphs.zh: 包括英国、法国和德国在内的其他国家也在大幅削减援助预算。英国于2025年2月宣布，援助预算将从国民总收入的0.5%降至2027年的0.3%，这是有记录以来占国民收入比例的最低水平。联合国的目标为0.7%。

paragraphs.en: Ivor Ichikowitz, whose South African family foundation commissioned the report, said: “The big picture [from the survey] is that the youth is concerned about governments that are overly influenced by foreign powers. What they’re saying is that African governments need to take agency and responsibility for their own reality.”
paragraphs.zh: 委托开展这项报告的南非家族基金会负责人伊沃尔·伊奇科维茨（Ivor Ichikowitz）表示：“（调查所反映的）大图景是，年轻人对受到外国势力过度影响的政府感到担忧。他们想说的是，非洲政府需要掌握主动权，为自己的现实承担责任。”

paragraphs.en: Africa has the youngest population in the world, with 70% of sub-Saharan Africa under the age of 30, according to the UN . The median age of the continent is 19 years and six months. By 2030, Africa will be home to more than 40% of the world’s youth .
paragraphs.zh: 根据联合国的数据，非洲是世界上人口最年轻的大陆，撒哈拉以南非洲70%的人口年龄在30岁以下。非洲大陆的中位年龄为19岁6个月。到2030年，非洲将拥有全球40%以上的青年人口。

paragraphs.en: The sudden USAID cuts were met with public outrage and pushback from development and humanitarian organisations. They caused the closure of vital services, including maternity clinics, and medicine shortages at a time when UN agencies are struggling to find money for their humanitarian work and food insecurity has been worsened by the climate crisis.
paragraphs.zh: 美国国际开发署突然削减援助引发了发展与人道主义组织的公愤和反对。这导致包括妇产诊所在内的关键服务关闭、药品短缺，而此时联合国各机构正难以为其人道主义工作筹集资金，气候危机又加剧了粮食不安全。

paragraphs.en: According to the survey, nearly half of African youth (46%) did believe the closure of USAID would have a damaging impact on their countries, with healthcare services and disease prevention seen as the areas most affected. This anxiety is highest in Mozambique (76%), followed by Kenya (63%) and Rwanda (63%), where youth feel the cuts will disproportionately affect the most vulnerable members of society.
paragraphs.zh: 调查显示，近半数的非洲青年（46%）确实认为美国国际开发署的关闭会对本国造成破坏性影响，其中医疗服务与疾病防控被视为受影响最严重的领域。这种担忧在莫桑比克最为强烈（76%），其次是肯尼亚（63%）和卢旺达（63%），这些国家的年轻人认为，削减援助将不成比例地影响社会中最脆弱的群体。
